title: AMA Wire: Survey quantifies time burdens of prior authorization (2017)

history.reason: Source read directly on access date; findings transcribed from the document.

source_type: News article by an advocacy organization reporting its own survey
reliability: Primary report of AMA's own web-based survey of 1,000 physicians (fielded December 2016). The AMA advocates for prior-authorization reform, so it is an interested party. Underlying questionnaire not examined.
findings: Web-based survey of 1,000 physicians administered in December (2016); respondents provided 20+ hours of care weekly and completed at least some prior-authorization (PA) requests.
Average of 37 PA requests per physician per week completed by physician and staff.
Average of 16.4 hours of physician and staff time per week spent on PA; 22% reported more than 20 hours.
About one-third of physicians have staff who work exclusively on PA.
75% rated the burden high or extremely high; 6% low or extremely low.
Fax and telephone were the most commonly reported ways to complete PA requests.
80% sometimes/often/always must repeat PA for patients already stabilized on a chronic treatment.
limitations: Data is from 2016; current conditions may differ.
Sample limited to physicians providing 20+ hours of care weekly who complete some PA; not all practices.
Article does not break results down by practice size or specialty.
